solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In US, hood needed in female group outside terminal in hail

indicators.note: the women's group sits around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a harem is the women of a household in a seraglio

indicators.note: the terminal letter of the word hail is its final one

explanation.surface: A group of women gathers round someone stuck at a terminal in a hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is American slang for neighbourhood; the New York district fits that, hence 'In US'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a well-known Manhattan neighbourhood, and hood is the American slang word for a district of a city.

clue.text: Flapper has dated grasping doctor after work

indicators.note: holding in its grip, so the old verb encloses the other pieces

parts.note: hath is the old form of has

indicators.note: the doctor comes after the work abbreviation

parts.note: wk is the abbreviation for work
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper's old-fashioned date clings to the doctor after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s young woman but here is a creature that flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawkmoth is a large, fast-flying moth, a winged insect that flaps, hence the jocular description.

clue.text: Left American feller resting in grass, carefree

indicators.note: the letters rest inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
ax is the American spelling of axe, a tool for felling trees

explanation.surface: A left-wing American chap lies in the grass without a care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like 'fellow' but means a thing that fells.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed means being at ease and untroubled, without worries.

clue.text: Green car briefly used in this person's sort of trade

parts.note: eco- means green, environmentally friendly

indicators.note: the short car name is placed inside the pronoun

parts.note: me is the pronoun for this person, the setter
a Merc is short for a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly car, used only briefly, is the setter's sort of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic trade carried out over the internet is one kind of commerce, buying and selling online.

clue.text: Poor toff's decline unseen by spectators

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the letters of toff's are put into disorder

parts.note: to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: An impoverished toff is going downhill, out of public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges TOFFS into OFFST; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything happening behind the scenes in a theatre, away from the audience's eyes, is happening in the wings.

clue.text: Supporting, on air, people counting votes in more than one medium

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting
an air is a tune
tellers count the votes in a parliamentary division

explanation.surface: Pundits on the radio back the vote-counters across more than one news outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like a means of communication, but a medium is a psychic, and the plural is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium claiming psychic powers foresees what lies ahead; mediums in plural are seers and clairvoyants.

clue.text: Current one sitting on the right avoids soup

indicators.note: the soup avoids the conservative, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: consommé is a clear soup
Con is short for a Conservative, someone on the political right

explanation.surface: A modern right-wing diner turns down the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present but is a flowing body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is a river in northern France, and a river is a current of water.

clue.text: Temporarily stop Jack getting into trouble on vessel

indicators.note: the jack's letter gets inside the fuss word

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
J is the card abbreviation for jack
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack runs into bother aboard a ship and has to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting or hearing is to suspend it until a later time.

clue.text: Recruit in US army maybe, sent from Dallas, showing guts

indicators.note: the guts of each word are its innermost letters, the middle pair

explanation.surface: A soldier dispatched from Texas proves courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' suggests courage but means insides; the middle two letters of each word are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist or sign up for military service is to join, here with the American double L spelling.

clue.text: Broadcast extra composed reptile recording from the 1980s

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: more composed, that is quieter and steadier
a chameleon is a colour-changing lizard

explanation.surface: A radio show plays a more relaxed piece about a reptile, recorded decades ago.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent 'calmer' sounds the same as KARMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Culture Club's 1983 chart-topping single is a well-known song from that decade.

clue.text: Going into work with Alan, unusually, I feel enlivened

indicators.note: the single letter of the clue's I is placed into the middle of the jumbled letters
done unusually means done in an odd way, so the letters of work and Alan are reordered

explanation.surface: Heading to the office with a colleague called Alan makes the speaker feel unexpectedly cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' looks like the definition's verb, but 'Going into' puts I inside WALKONAR, which is what 'unusually' makes of the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being so elated that one seems to float, which is feeling thoroughly enlivened and happy.

clue.text: Start to judge soldiers after retreating, AM and PM

indicators.note: the initial letter of judge and the soldiers come after the turned-round pair
something retreating goes back, so the two letters of AM are read in the other direction
the start of the word judge is its first letter

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A judge's day starts with soldiers falling back, morning and afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AM and PM' looks like a pair of times of day; AM is wordplay and PM means Prime Minister, John Major having led Britain 1990-97.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major was the British Prime Minister in the 1990s, so the surname serves for a PM.

clue.text: Before mountaineer's original show of hesitation, skirt peak

indicators.note: the skirt comes before the letter and the hesitation sound

parts.note: a maxi is a long skirt

indicators.note: the original letter of mountaineer's is its opening one

parts.note: um is the noise people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A climber dithers before tackling the summit in a long skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or greatest amount of something is its peak, used as a noun.

clue.text: A Parisian international out of game's uniform? Not so

parts.note: une is the French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: the international's letter is taken out of the bird

parts.note: the quail is a game bird

explanation.surface: A French international player is dropped from a match because of his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like sports kit but is the adjective meaning even; 'Not so' negates it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not uniform is uneven or irregular, varying in size or amount.

clue.text: Gold located on ground, announced upper-class family

indicators.note: the sounded syllable has the gold placed on its end
spoken out loud, the word for ground by teeth gives the first syllable

parts.note: ground with the teeth, as food is when it is chewed
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold found lying on the ground is publicly reported by a posh family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the past of grind, as with teeth (chewed), not earth; 'Gold located on' puts OR after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal house of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, about as upper-class as a family gets.

clue.text: Sports supplement given around Aintree to jockey

parts.note: c, short for circa, means around

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters of Aintree are shifted about

explanation.surface: A sports supplement is handed out round the racecourse at Aintree for a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National; 'to jockey' rearranges it into REATINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatine is an amino-acid compound taken by athletes to build muscle, a common sports supplement.

clue.text: Drug squad suppressing network quietly

indicators.note: holding down and containing, so the squad word encloses the rest

parts.note: a squad is a team
a maze is a network of paths
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A drug squad quietly shuts down a dealing network.
explanation.definitionFit: Temazepam is a benzodiazepine sedative prescribed for insomnia, a medicinal drug.

clue.text: Sheryl getting renovated bags with diamonds, showing Prudence

indicators.note: to bag is to take or hold, so the reworked letters hold the others
something renovated is done over and remade, so the letters of Sheryl are rearranged

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Sheryl, having had a makeover, carries diamond-studded handbags, flaunting them in front of her friend Prudence.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Prudence look like a name; it means good sense. 'renovated' turns SHERYL into SHRELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting shrewdly means acting with astute good judgment, which is what showing prudence describes.

clue.text: Live idly in car, renouncing son — squash perhaps at first

indicators.note: the vegetables come at the beginning

parts.note: squash is one example of veg, short for vegetables

indicators.note: giving something up, so the son's letter is dropped from the car

parts.note: an estate is an estate car, a station wagon
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone lounges in a car, disowning a son, with squash as the first meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S from ESTATE leaves ETATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vegetate is to lead a dull, inactive life, doing little but sitting about.

clue.text: Perhaps Bruce's rabbit finding slug beneath some corn

indicators.note: in this down entry the hitting word goes below the corn

parts.note: an ear is a head of corn
to slug someone is to hit them, to bash

explanation.surface: An Australian's pet rabbit finds a slug under a cornstalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bruce' is the stock nickname for an Australian man, and 'rabbit' is British slang for chatter on endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian slang word means to talk at someone incessantly, which Britons call rabbiting on.

clue.text: Some bush trimming brought about hilarity

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, as a ship is, so the letters run backwards
only some of the letters across the words bush trimming are used

explanation.surface: Pruning a shrub caused great amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes HTRIM from 'busH TRIMming', and 'brought about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is merriment and laughter, a direct synonym for hilarity.

clue.text: French firm about line being used among tuna at sea

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the line is used in among the confused letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of tuna are scrambled

explanation.surface: A French company is involved with a fishing line among tuna in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns TUNA into NAUT, and L goes in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Renault is the French car manufacturer, so it is a company from France.

clue.text: Endure underlying smell going round old Soviet district

indicators.note: in the down entry the enduring word lies beneath the turned-round smell
turning round means the two letters of the smell are read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour
to last is to endure

explanation.surface: People put up with an unpleasant smell spreading through an old Soviet area.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblast was an administrative region of the USSR, and the word is still used in Russia and Ukraine.

clue.text: Two different bands with what Spanish artistic style?

parts.note: a bar is a band or stripe, and the letter O is shaped like a ring or band
que is the Spanish for what

explanation.surface: Two separate musical groups play together in some Spanish art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' looks like groups of musicians but means a stripe and a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque is the ornate seventeenth-century European style of art, architecture and music.

clue.text: Waiters in Queen's Head repeatedly upset community

indicators.note: the head of the word Queen's is its first letter
the turned-round pair is used twice
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: EU is the European Union, once the European Community

explanation.surface: Bar staff at a pub called the Queen's Head keep upsetting the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiters' suggests restaurant staff but means people waiting in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn is a queue, so those in it are waiters.

clue.text: Enter captivating religious school and note quadrangle?

indicators.note: holding something captive, so the record word encloses the religious school

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
Zen is a school of Buddhism
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a charming college and notices its courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quadrangle' suggests a college courtyard but means a four-sided figure, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a diamond-shaped figure, a rhombus, which has four sides and four angles.

clue.text: Master describes annual fast

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw round, so the expert goes round the yearly letters

parts.note: an ace is a master or expert
p.a. is per annum, yearly

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster talks about a fast held once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like the noun for not eating but is the adverb meaning quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means at speed, swiftly, so it matches fast used as an adverb.

clue.text: American writer, unknown, in time associated with pen

indicators.note: the unknown sits in the middle of the period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
z is a mathematical unknown
a pound is an enclosure or pen for animals

explanation.surface: An obscure American author was linked for a time with a particular pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American Modernist poet, so he is a writer from the United States.

clue.text: Eighteen, rebelliously expressing derision

indicators.note: behaving rebelliously means refusing to keep order, so the letters of eighteen are reordered

explanation.surface: An eighteen-year-old rebel sneers at authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggling in a mocking, sniggering way is a way of showing scorn for someone.

clue.text: With my involvement, suspect this forger seen here

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of my and this are placed in doubtful order

explanation.surface: With my help, the police suspect this man of being a counterfeiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' looks like a counterfeiter but is a blacksmith who forges metal; 'With ... involvement' adds MY to THIS for the 'suspect' rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, so it is where someone working metal at a forge is found.
